reviews.title: Very disappointed, Customer Service should have done better
reviews.text:
I ordered a canvas as a Christmas gift for my daughter featuring her two dogs. I spent over $100 on this canvas, only to receive a finished product where an ear was cut off and the paws on both dogs were cut off.
I contacted Ronald at customer service immediately and provided my order ID. They told me that they reviewed my image and that the problem occurred because I selected the “full bleed” layout. They explained that the image wraps around the frame and may unintentionally crop parts of the photo.
My question is: How was I supposed to know that?
I am not a photographer or a professional in photo printing. When I was creating my canvas, there was no clear warning telling me that selecting this option could cut off important parts of the subjects in my photograph. If I had been properly warned, I would have chosen a different layout.
Instead, I paid over $100 for a Christmas gift that is not acceptable. These aren’t insignificant details—the ear and paws of the dogs are actually missing from the finished picture.
What is most disappointing is the customer service response. Rather than taking responsibility for a problem that was not clearly explained during the ordering process, they essentially told me that I selected the wrong option and refused to correct the problem.
I believe the company should replace this canvas at no charge. I paid for a finished canvas that would properly display the photograph I submitted. If your ordering process allows an image to be cropped in

reviews.title: Do yourself a favour and avoid this App on iOS
reviews.text:
If you want to share photos fom iOS with someone on Android, better create a shared Album iOS Photos App and create a public link and share via WhatsApp or Mail.

iOS Google Photos App syncs all photos in itself and starts backing up to your Google Account and you will run out of space in no time, which will force you to buy more storage on google Account.

Warning: If you remove photos from Google Photos App, it will also remove them from your iOS library as well. If you don’t recover them from iOS ‘Recently Deleted’ album within 30 days, photos will be gone forever.

If you stop backup, the Album you share with someone will show photos in the App for you but not to the person you share the album with.

Even when you share an album with someone, that person will neither get a mail nor a notification in his or her Android Photos App so there will be no way to access the shred album.

You may create a sharable link from Google Photos App but as indicated, if the photos in shred album were not backed up to your google account, the photos will not be visible to the person opening the link.

This App is the most poorly conceived App that I’ve ever seen.

Google just thought of hijacking your photos from iOS library without not making it very transparent.

Avoid yourself a lot of heartache and stay away from this App on iOS.

reviews.title: Would have given ZERO stars
reviews.text:
I’ve used GP for many years, always loved it. I’ve worked around many of its quirky features over the years, but now im done with it. I’ll be moving all of my photos out and cancelling my subscription. 

I understand there are good reasons for managing space on my phone, stored in GP, clear space on your phone. I get it. 

How about this, GIVE ME THE OPTION OF DECIDING IF I WANT TO DELETE EVERY COPY FROM ALL DEVICES AND OTHER CLOUD SERVICES??!!

I have more than one GP account as I use Google to have my business account too. 
Can I stop my personal photos appearing in my Business Photos??? 
NO I CANT - because it gives GP access to every single area of my accounts to import every photo regardless if I want my business account to have them or not. 
If I choose to stop syncing - guess what, it stops syncing FOR MY PERSONAL GMAIL TOO!!! 

So it’s either all or nothing. Either I allow all photos to sync to my personal Gmail and work Gmail or I turn off syncing. 
And if I have the temerity to want to delete my PERSONAL photos from my work Gmail, IT WANTS TO DELETE MY PERSONAL PHOTO FROM EVERYWHERE!!!!

Google, I’ve been with you for many years. 
Why are you so jealous of me having photos that I don’t share with you? 
Why do you take away my choice of where I want to store photos? 

You make it either all or nothing. 

I’m now choosing nothing.

reviews.text:
Dear Google Photos Team,

I’m genuinely frustrated with how Google Photos works on iPhone.

I use Google Photos specifically because I want my Google Photos library to remain separate from my iPhone’s Apple Photos library. I do NOT want Google Photos to automatically access, mix, or back up the photos currently stored on my iPhone.

I’m completely fine with Google Photos having access to the photos that are already stored in my Google account. What I’m NOT fine with is having to give the Google Photos app Full Access to my iPhone Photos library just to properly view my existing Google Photos library.

This creates a ridiculous choice:

* Give Google Photos Full Access → risk my iPhone photos being backed up/mixed into Google Photos and consuming my Google storage.
* Give Google Photos Limited Access → the app becomes frustratingly limited and doesn’t properly show my existing Google Photos experience.

And then, once someone’s Google storage fills up because Photos has backed up their iPhone library, Google starts warning that Gmail and other services may be affected unless they purchase additional storage.

Why can’t Google Photos simply let me access my existing Google Photos cloud library without requiring access to my entire Apple Photos library?

I should be able to say:

“Show me the photos already stored in my Google account. Do not access or back up anything from my iPhone unless I explicitly choose to upload it.”

That seems like a basic privacy and product-design re

I restored them from my bin but it never restored them back to my iPhone. There is no way to clean up memory by deleting photos within google photos. It also deletes it from your iPhone. So you have to do that first and then go to your bin and one by one download it to your iPhone again and then one by one download them back to your phone. Oh but guess what, when you delete them again it will delete it from your iPhones own memory. So once your photos are on this app,you can never remove them without them being removed from your phone entirely. Great app guys. Are you guys beginners or something?
